'''''Malva hispanica''''', the '''Spanish mallow''', is a species of flowering plant in the family [[Malvaceae]], native to the western Mediterranean.<ref name="561701-1" >{{cite web |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:561701-1 |title=''Malva hispanica'' L. |author=<!--Not stated--> |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=Board of Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=15 June 2021 }}</ref> Uniquely in its genus, ''Malva hispanica'' flowers possess a bilobed [[epicalyx]], which is derived from an ancestral trimerous structure and represents a loss of the adaxial epicalyx lobe.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Floral development of ''Lavatera trimestris'' and ''Malva hispanica'' reveals the nature of the epicalyx in the ''Malva'' generic alliance |year=2016 |last1=Bello |first1=María A. |last2=Martínez-Asperilla |first2=Aránzazu |last3=Fuertes-Aguilar |first3=Javier |journal=Botanical Journal of the Linnean Society |volume=181 |pages=84–98 |doi=10.1111/boj.12391 |doi-access=free }}</ref>
